A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSR associative-memory work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original memory-count simulations, Gaussian-mixture log-likelihood experiments, and MNIST/TinyImagenet generation results in Figures 3–4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds kernel-landscape comparisons, pixel-space MNIST emergence, and a 60,000-image MNIST experiment.

M1.justification: The LSR energy in Equation (3) and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same fixed-point retrieval, temperature search and memory-enumeration procedures. Alternative kernels are comparative analyses; the biological implementation passage provides a conceptual mapping.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic hypercube/Gaussian-mixture data, MNIST and TinyImagenet for memory emergence, retrieval and generation. The added MNIST experiments vary representation and sample count within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 6 substantially broadens the emergence comparison beyond LSR versus Gaussian/LSE to triangle, uniform, quartic, triweight, tricube and cosine kernels. Their appearance in v1 Figure 5 concerned kernel shapes and KDE efficiency; their memory-landscape behavior is newly compared.

E3.justification: Added protocols include an eight-image normalized-pixel ablation, comparisons across kernels and temperatures, and storage of all 60,000 MNIST training images. The latter selects beta for approximately 50% retrievability and samples memories near a seed image instead of exhaustively enumerating them. These extend the evaluation design substantially.

E4.justification: Appendix C/Figure 6 newly examines kernel dependence and basin merging. Appendix D.5/Figure 9 ablates the VAE to expose pixel-space centroid formation, while D.6/Figure 10 examines emergence with substantially more stored patterns. These address questions absent from v1's analyses.

E5.justification: The Gaussian-mixture experiments retain five random seeds, the same standard-error reporting, and the same alignment of temperature indices across seeds. The added demonstrations introduce no new repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Existing plotted results remain unchanged. New findings include kernel-dependent emergence, with none observed for triweight in the examined settings; eight pixel-space emergent memories alongside eight retrievable originals; and a 60,000-image example with approximately 50% retrievability and 16 displayed emergent memories near one seed. These substantially extend the reported findings.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–3, Theorems 1–2, Propositions 1–3 and their proofs are mathematically unchanged. The proofs move from Appendix D to Appendix E. The new kernel and biological discussions are qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: exponential capacity with exact retrieval, simultaneous stored and emergent memories, comparable Gaussian-mixture log-likelihood, and plausible latent-space image generations.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's existing finite-support and centroid/latent-space limitations, v2 adds substantial interpretation in Section 5 and Appendices B–C. It discusses application-dependent usefulness, blurry generations, hallucination analogies, biological implementation and weight symmetry, and kernel-specific emergence mechanisms and uncertainties.

D1.justification: v2 reports a linked public GitHub codebase instead of a submitted supplementary ZIP and expands image-selection, normalization and shape details in D.4. Existing hardware, runtimes and VAE hyperparameters remain. The newly stated MNIST matrix shape, 24 x 768, conflicts with the retained 10-dimensional latent description.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Rombach et al. latent-diffusion reference and associated TAESD provenance sentence. Appendix B.2 newly connects LSR to the biological-network mapping of existing reference 8. The principal related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: v2 adds dedicated Discussion and Extended Discussion sections, reorganizes the qualitative-reconstruction appendix around energy construction and memory discovery, and makes localized prose and caption edits. Most existing exposition, including the introduction and theoretical development, remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adopts NeurIPS formatting with a redesigned title/author block and denser typography throughout. It adds the kernel-landscape grid and two image figures, relocates existing figures, and places the retained Gaussian-mixture appendix plots together as Figures 7–8. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The kernel comparisons, pixel-space ablation and larger-memory example provide useful additional support, while the expanded discussion clarifies applicability and the code link improves access. The gains are mostly illustrative; the central theory and quantitative comparisons remain unchanged. The new dimensional inconsistency in D.4 limits the reproducibility improvement, but the net benefit is modestly positive.
